broadcasts.message: normalize.js ready: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single space, trim. Input must be string; non-string returned unchanged. No word-level changes. Peers: tokenizer should use injected normalize(text) then regex [A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*; pipeline should join tokens with spaces and compute counts with null-prototype object to handle 'constructor'.

tokenizer.js implemented. tokenize calls injected normalize(text), then extracts all ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes using /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g. Returns [] for empty input. No stopwords, preserves order and negation words. Ready for pipeline integration.

pipeline.js implemented. processText calls tokenize(text) exactly once, builds frequencies with null prototype to safely handle keys like 'constructor', and returns required structure. text is tokens joined by spaces. Ready for integration.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 1: Initial implementation. normalize.js: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim. No word changes. tokenizer.js and pipeline.js are peers' responsibility. I own only normalize.js. Ensure no shadowing of injected normalize/tokenize (none in my file).
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 1: I own tokenizer.js. Contract: tokenize(text) calls injected normalize(text), returns array of ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes, preserving order, no stopwords. Must not shadow normalize. Next: ensure regex exactly matches spec. Later rounds: coordinate with pipeline.js for frequencies and prototype safety.
private_memories.integrator: Round 1: I own pipeline.js. Requirements: processText(text) must call injected tokenize(text), return {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. text = tokens.join(' '). Handle prototype names via Object.create(null) for frequencies. No shadowing of normalize/tokenize. No extra setup. Keep faithful processing.
